description: A workspace of one million documents with no text at all, sitting exactly on the document-count resource limit. It costs the customer nothing and costs Koru a great deal. The case exists to prove that billing and resource limits are two mechanisms, not one: zero cost, and a clear refusal.
notes: Two assertions about the same workspace at the same moment: logical_usage_units is ZERO, and a new document's first durable receipt is REFUSED with WORKSPACE_DOCUMENT_LIMIT_REACHED. An implementation that cannot produce both simultaneously has merged two mechanisms that must stay apart.
The input is parametric rather than enumerated: writing 1 000 000 identical documents out would make the file unreadable without making it more precise.
Billing: 0 LU. Not a rounding, not a floor - zero. Structure is free (D79) and this workspace is nothing but structure.

The resource limit does not appear anywhere in the arithmetic. The usage number here is identical to what it would be with no limit configured at all; that is what makes it a resource limit rather than a quota rule (contract 7.2).

The limit shown is the contract-recommended 1 000 000 documents per workspace, with the workspace sitting exactly on it. The 10% and 50% alert thresholds (100 000 and 500 000) fired long ago and refused nothing - they are the warning, not the wall.
Narrowness matters: local editing is unaffected, the 1 000 000 existing documents keep syncing, their files keep uploading, and only the first durable receipt for a NEW document is refused.
Recovery is live. Deleting documents brings the workspace back under and Cloud resumes by itself - no reset, no ticket, no clock.

NON-NORMATIVE: the v1 revision would have charged 64 per node, so this workspace would have read 6 400 000 and quota would have bounded the cardinality by itself. It no longer does, which is exactly why the limit had to be defined.

configured_resource_limits.note: a named threshold in configuration (contract 7.3); the CTO confirms the value at approval

attempted_operation.operation: first durable Cloud receipt for a document not already in the workspace's durable set

derivation: each document: 1 node, kind task, text "" -> no authored text; structure, marks, references and non-text values are free = 0
resource limit (a separate mechanism; contributes nothing to the line above):
the attempted operation creates a document not already in the durable set -> REFUSED

operational: document cardinality 1000000 for one workspace; physical-to-logical ratio is unbounded (a non-zero physical footprint over a zero logical one). Both are contract 7.1 quantities and both alert well before the limit.

billing.note: unchanged by the presence of the resource limit; the limit is not a term in the formula

resource_limit.refused: the first durable Cloud receipt for a document not already in the workspace's durable set
allowed: durable receipts for the 1 000 000 documents already in the durable set
blob uploads for documents already in the durable set
message_must_name: the two ways out: remove documents, or use another workspace
resource_limit.recovery: live - deleting documents brings the workspace back under and Cloud resumes by itself
is_not: WORKSPACE_LIMIT_REACHED - that is D34's optional allowance ceiling, a different thing with a similar name

operational_signals_required.requirement: measured continuously, alert thresholds at 10% and 50% of the limit, so an account approaching the wall is visible long before it arrives
measured continuously, named threshold in configuration, alerts when crossed

must_not: let the limit change the usage number by any amount
refuse without the stable code and a product-visible message - a silent accounting limit is forbidden
refuse anything local, or anything about documents already in the durable set
